keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Masterclass in modern progressive rock songwriting, combining shifting time signatures (7/4, 3/4, 4/4), wide-interval ringing suspended chords, and one of the most emotional, expressive whammy bar guitar solos in rock history
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: C# minor is the relative minor

mainProgression.description: Ringing open string chord voicings with shifting time signatures and melodic arpeggios.

sectionProgressions.description: Alex Lifeson's signature 'Hentor Sportscaster' open string voicings cycling through alternating meters
Smooth descending diatonic bassline supporting Geddy Lee's introspective lyrical delivery
Alex Lifeson's self-professed favorite guitar solo, isolated in the mix with ethereal delay and whammy bar vibrato

harmonicFunction: E (I) - Luminous, triumphant tonic reinforced by ringing open B and high E strings
Aadd9 (IVadd9) - Subdominant chord enriched with the 9th (B) providing spacious harmonic shimmer
F#7add11 (II7add11) - Secondary dominant with open string extensions providing forward harmonic pull
Bsus4 (Vsus4) - Suspended dominant resolving cleanly into the E major tonic

techniques.name: Asymmetric Meter Shifts & Whammy Bar Expressive Phrasing
techniques.description: Mastering the seamless transition between 7/4, 3/4, and 4/4 time signatures while picking wide-interval open string extensions, followed by lyrical whammy bar articulation in the solo

notes: Open string voicings: Keep the open B and high E strings ringing freely across all chord shapes
7/4 counting: Counted as a bar of 4/4 followed by a bar of 3/4 (1-2-3-4, 1-2-3)
Whammy bar articulation: Depress the tremolo arm slightly before picking and release it to pitch, creating a vocal sigh
sequence: Memorize the signature chord voicings with ringing top strings (Aadd9, F#7add11, Bsus4)
Count the intro time signature shifts out loud with a metronome at 132 BPM
Practice alternate picking through the arpeggiated figures to ensure clean string separation
Incorporate subtle Floyd Rose / synchronized tremolo dips to shape notes in the solo
tips: Use your thumb over the top of the neck to fret bass notes while freeing lower fingers for chord extensions
Do not mute the open top two strings—they are the sonic glue that ties the entire song together
Apply an analog delay set to approximately 350ms to recreate the spacious studio aura of Le Studio

techniques.name: Open-String Voicings with Ringing Drone B/E Strings
techniques.description: Executing Alex Lifeson's trademark wide-interval chords (F#7add11, Aadd9, Bsus4) that leave strings 1 and 2 open as constant ringing drone unisons and fifths

notes: F#7add11 voicing: 2-4-4-3-0-0 (thumb over on low F#)
Bsus4 voicing: X-2-4-4-0-0
Harmonic function: The open B and E provide continuous luminous shimmer regardless of the bass root
sequence: Arch fretting fingers carefully so the underside of the index and middle fingers never brush strings 1 and 2
Practice shifting between F#7add11 and Bsus4 without interrupting the drone resonance
Strum with a medium-light pick (0.73mm) for balanced acoustic-like chime through cranked Marshall stacks
Coordinate the dynamic swell when dropping from loud chorus chords into the delicate verse arpeggios
tips: Check each string individually to verify that the high open E and B strings ring completely true without buzzing
Use chorus effect (Roland CE-1 or Boss CE-2) to widen the stereo field across the ringing open intervals
Allow the open strings to sustain across the bar lines to smooth over the metric transitions

sections.name: Asymmetric Intro Riff (7/4 & 3/4 Meter Shifts)
sections.description: Alex Lifeson's genius open-chord riff that serves as the dynamic and harmonic anchor of the song.
notes: Count the alternating 7/4 (4+3) and 3/4 bars carefully
Keep open B and high E strings ringing freely
Lock tightly with Neil Peart's syncopated ride cymbal bell

sections.name: Verse 1 Diatonic Groove & Introspective Chords (4/4)
sections.technique: Descending Diatonic Voice Leading & Subtle Muting
sections.description: The song transitions into straight 4/4 time with a delicate descending progression (E - B/D# - C#m - A) underneath Geddy Lee's introspective vocal.
notes: Smooth transition into straight 4/4 time
Gentle pick attack to let the vocal dominate
Descending bass line on strings 5 and 6

sections.name: Anthemic Chorus ('Living in the limelight, the universal dream')
sections.description: The triumphant chorus explosion featuring Lifeson's expansive open chords driven by aggressive downstrokes and soaring bass counter-melodies.
notes: Maximum right-hand strumming power
Open high strings ring above the rhythm section
Triumphant melodic resolution

sections.name: Verse 2 Layered Guitars & Geddy Lee Counterpoint
sections.description: Second verse featuring subtle guitar fills and shimmering chorus pedal textures weaving around Geddy's bass lines.
notes: Delicate picking across the middle strings
Leave acoustic space for the bass guitar counterpoint
Maintain steady 4/4 pulse

sections.name: Alex Lifeson Lyrical Whammy Bar Solo
sections.technique: Vocal Whammy Bar Articulation & Ethereal Phrasing
sections.description: One of the most praised guitar solos in rock history, celebrated for its emotional depth, Floyd Rose scooping, and melodic purity.
notes: Whammy bar scoops on initial note strikes
Singing vibrato with long analog delay repeats
E Lydian raised 4th (A#) color note

sections.name: Final Chorus & Ringing Suspended Outro Cadence
sections.technique: Asymmetric Cadence & Ringing E Major Fade
sections.description: The climatic final chorus returning to the 7/4 and 3/4 asymmetric riff motif, culminating in a ringing suspended chord fadeout.
notes: Seamless return from 4/4 chorus to 7/4 intro riff
Full band intensity through the final cadence
Let the final E major chord ring with stereo chorus

guitar.recommended: 'Hentor Sportscaster' (Modified Stratocaster with Bill Lawrence L-500 humbucker & Floyd Rose tremolo) / Gibson ES-335
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker with biting output, paired with single-coil chime on rhythm tracks

amp.recommended: Marshall JMP 100-watt / Hiwatt Custom 100 through Mesa/Boogie 4x12 cabinet

effects.distortion: Marshall tube preamp crunch layered with pristine clean headroom
effects.reverb: Large hall reverb simulating the ambient stone acoustics of Le Studio, Morin-Heights
effects.other: Floyd Rose / Strat tremolo bridge for subtle pitch modulation
effects.chorus: Roland CE-1 / Boss CE-2 for signature lush, wide stereo shimmer
effects.delay: Stereo tape delay set to 350ms on the solo

beginner.title: Chord Voicings & Drone Strings
steps: Learn the fingerings for Aadd9, F#7add11, and Bsus4
Ensure the high B and E strings ring cleanly without fret buzz or finger muting
Practice strumming the basic verse progression in standard 4/4 time

intermediate.title: Asymmetric Counting & Intro Riff
steps: Count the 7/4 and 3/4 meter shifts smoothly with a metronome
Alternate pick through the arpeggiated intro pattern at 110 BPM before pushing to 132 BPM
Lock into Neil Peart's drum accents and Geddy Lee's driving bass line

advanced.title: Whammy Bar Solo Articulation & Nuance
steps: Learn Alex Lifeson's solo phrasing, paying close attention to micro-tonal pitch bends
Use the whammy bar to scoop into notes and create smooth, vocal vibrato
Balance pick dynamics and delay trails to allow sustained notes to bloom naturally

commonMistakes: Muting the high open E and B strings with the fretting fingers on F#7add11 and Bsus4
Losing track of the beat count during the shift between 7/4 and 3/4 measures
Over-using the whammy bar in the solo instead of executing subtle, controlled vocal vibrato
practiceRoutine: 15 minutes: Open-string chord transitions with ringing top drone strings
15 minutes: Metronome practice on the 7/4 and 3/4 asymmetric counting at 110-132 BPM
10 minutes: Whammy bar pitch control and delayed note sustain in the solo
focusAreas: Open B and high E drone string clarity
Metric stability across time signature shifts
metronomeWork: Practice 7/4 as 4 beats + 3 beats at 110, 120, and 132 BPM
